item.title: “Migajāla, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in them, praises…
item.description:
“Migajāla, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in them, praises them, and dwells with lust for them, then because he delights, praises, and dwells with lust, delight arises. With the arising of delight, lust arises. With the arising of lust, bondage arises. Bound by the bondage of delight, Migajāla, that monk is called ‘one who dwells with a companion.’ Even if he lives in remote lodgings, in forests, in groves, in quiet places, with little sound, little noise, free from people’s breath, secluded, suitable for seclusion — still he is called ‘one who dwells with a companion.’ Why? Because craving, the companion, has not been abandoned by him. Therefore he is called ‘one who dwells with a companion.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.63
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, and has no tendency towards anything, there is no basis for the establishment of consciousness. When…
item.description:
“Monks, if one does not intend, does not plan, and has no tendency towards anything, there is no basis for the establishment of consciousness. When there is no basis, consciousness does not become established. When consciousness is not established and does not grow, there is no production of future renewed existence. When there is no future renewed existence, future birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair cease. Such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.38
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “And, Migajāla, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable … enticing. If a monk does not delight in them, does not praise…
item.description:
“And, Migajāla, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable … enticing. If a monk does not delight in them, does not praise them, and dwells without lust for them, then because he does not delight, does not praise, and dwells without lust, delight ceases. With the cessation of delight, lust ceases. With the cessation of lust, bondage ceases. Not being bound by the bondage of delight, Migajāla, that monk is called ‘one who dwells alone.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.63
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monks, one who dwells seeing gratification in things that are fetters — greed is not abandoned, hatred is not abandoned, delusion is not abandoned. Because…
item.description:
“Monks, one who dwells seeing gratification in things that are fetters — greed is not abandoned, hatred is not abandoned, delusion is not abandoned. Because greed, hatred, and delusion are not abandoned, he is not freed from birth, aging, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. I say that he is not freed from suffering.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 2.6
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “When, monks, a monk is not lustful regarding objects that can provoke lust, and his self is free from lust; is not hateful regarding objects…
item.description:
“When, monks, a monk is not lustful regarding objects that can provoke lust, and his self is free from lust; is not hateful regarding objects that can provoke hatred, and his self is free from hatred; is not deluded regarding objects that can provoke delusion, and his self is free from delusion; is not infatuated regarding objects that can provoke infatuation, and his self is free from infatuation — then he has no fear, no trembling, no terror, does not fall into fear, and does not go by whatever ascetics may say.”

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.117
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: “Monk, I say that there are these three feelings: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. These three feelings have been spoken of by me. But,…
item.description:
“Monk, I say that there are these three feelings: pleasant feeling, painful feeling, neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. These three feelings have been spoken of by me. But, monk, I also say: ‘Whatever is felt is included in suffering.’ It is in relation to the impermanence of formations that this is said: ‘Whatever is felt is included in suffering.’ It is in relation to the nature of destruction, the nature of vanishing, the nature of fading away, the nature of cessation, the nature of change of formations that this is said: ‘Whatever is felt is included in suffering.’”

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 36.11
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Suffering from disease and aging, And also subject to death — Such is the nature of conditioned things, Such is the nature of beings. If…
item.description:
Suffering from disease and aging,
And also subject to death —
Such is the nature of conditioned things,
Such is the nature of beings.
If ordinary people become disenchanted,
That would not be fitting for me —
If I too were disenchanted
With beings who share the same fate.
While I live,
Not different from them,
I dwell thus,
Knowing the Dhamma without attachment.
Conceit in health,
In youth, in life —
All these I have subdued,
Springing from security.
I see the path of seclusion,
I arouse strong energy,
Seeing the state of Nibbāna.
Now I cannot
Enjoy sensual pleasures —
I will not fall back,
Achieving the final goal of the holy life.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.57
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Who once was heedless, but later is not, Illuminates this world like the moon freed from clouds. Whoever stops an evil deed by a wholesome…
item.description:
Who once was heedless, but later is not,
Illuminates this world like the moon freed from clouds.
Whoever stops an evil deed by a wholesome one,
Illuminates this world like the moon freed from clouds.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 86 – Aṅgulimālasutta
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: Elder Māluṅkyaputta: One who lives heedlessly, Craving grows like a creeper. He drifts and wanders, Life after life, Like a monkey in the forest, Longing…
item.description:
Elder Māluṅkyaputta:

One who lives heedlessly,
Craving grows like a creeper.
He drifts and wanders,
Life after life,
Like a monkey in the forest,
Longing for fruit.

This wretched craving
Poisons the whole world.
When it conquers anyone,
Sorrow increases —
Like birana grass
Spreading and growing.

One who subdues craving,
Wretched, hard to conquer —
Sorrow falls from that person
Like a water drop from a lotus.

You have come here —
I teach this good thing.
Dig up the root of craving
Like seeking the sweet root
Of the usīra grass.
Do not let Māra, the flood,
Destroy you like a reed,
Again and again, forever.

Practice the Buddha’s instruction.
Do not let the moment pass.
If the moment passes, sorrow,
You will suffer in hell.

Heedlessness is dust,
Filthy dust born of heedlessness.
Heedful, with clear wisdom,
Pull out the dart from yourself.

From: Theragāthā 6.5
📖 Read this sutta

item.title: One whose mind inclines to renunciation, His heart tends toward seclusion; One whose mind inclines to non-ill-will, His heart tends toward the cessation of clinging;…
item.description:
One whose mind inclines to renunciation,
His heart tends toward seclusion;
One whose mind inclines to non-ill-will,
His heart tends toward the cessation of clinging;
One whose mind inclines to the cessation of craving,
His heart tends toward the absence of delusion;
Seeing the place of arising,
His mind is rightly liberated.
For one rightly liberated,
The monk with a pure mind,
There is nothing further to do,
Nothing remains to be done.
Like a solid mass of rock,
Unmoved by the wind,
So too, all forms,
Tastes, sounds, smells, contacts,
And all phenomena —
Agreeable or disagreeable —
Cannot disturb one such as this,
Whose mind is steady, liberated,
Seeing the nature of their cessation.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.55
📖 Read this sutta
